sources.citation: Zhang, Yijia; Jin, Xiaoyu; Liu, Li. 2023. Palatalization in Laomian: evolution and resistance. Humanities and Social Sciences Communications 10:425. doi:10.1057/s41599-023-01899-1
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Gives the Laomian (Lancang) onset inventory (Table 1, based on Xu 1998 cross-checked with the first author's field data) and cites forms with Chao tone digits (55, 33, 31); no mention of stress or accent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent and read). States that the Laomian data derive from Xu Shixuan 1998 Bisuyu yanjiu, i.e. Xu's 'Bisu' = Laomian of Lancang.

sources.citation: Tun, Maung Maung. 2014. A sociolinguistic survey of selected Bisoid varieties: Pyen, Laomian and Laopin. MA thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai. 301 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Laomian/Laopin. Sociolinguistic survey with 462-item wordlists; ch.2 reviews Pyen phonology after Person 2007 (C1(C2)VT(C3), three tones) and Xu 2001 on Laomian/Laopin language use; the only 'stress patterns' mention (p.11) refers to Vacharee Nuamkaew 1987 on Thailand Bisu.

sources.citation: Person, Kirk R. 2007. A preliminary phonological sketch of Pyen, with comparison to Bisu. SEALS XIII, 193-201. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics. [Pyen, pyen1239, sister variety]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Per the held scanned (a full-text search for stress/accent): three contrastive tones, tone obligatory on every syllable; no mention of Laomian and no stress statement.

sources.citation: Kitjapol Udomkool. 2006. A phonological comparison of selected Bisoid speech varieties. MA thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai. 207 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing (no occurrence of stress/accent). Laomian and Laopin enter only the lexicostatistic comparison (wordlists supplied by K. Person); the phonological descriptions proper (syllable types, segments, tones by syllable position) cover Bantang, Thailand Bisu, Cauho and Tsukong; the conclusion recommends a future comparison of Laomian, Laopin and Tsukong phonology.

sources.citation: Sagart, Laurent. 2003. A new collection of descriptions of languages of China [review of the Zhongguo xin faxian yuyan yanjiu congshu]. Cahiers de Linguistique Asie Orientale 32(2): 287-298.
sources.note: Persee HTML read (PDF download 403): mentions the Bisu volume (Xu 1998) only in the list of the twelve volumes; nothing on Bisu prosody in the visible text.

sources.citation: Nishida, Tatsuo. 1973. A preliminary study on the Bisu language: a language of Northern Thailand, recently discovered by us. Pacific Linguistics A-30: 55-82. [Ban Lua Bisu, Thailand = bisu1244, closely related variety]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No word-stress rule. Sec. 4 Toneme (pp.58-60): register tones high/mid/low; notes 'weak utterances' of subordinate morphemes following a 'main syllable' and tonal 'modulation' of bound morphemes, i.e. root-syllable prominence is implied but stress is never named. Not Laomian.
